purpose: Research-only evidence candidates; no canonical or runtime promotion.

species.remainingGap: Adult wild telemetry provides an encountered range, but the study reports little behavioral response to temperature and does not estimate selection or preference.
Korean field tags recorded adult-sized fish temperatures, but only individual means and variability were reported; no population min/max selection function was estimated.

A peer-reviewed paper states that schools select 10-20 degC coastal water, but the statement is background context rather than a documented adult selection analysis; modern adult tags report exposure and cold avoidance without a selected min/max range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Estimation of the Metabolic Rate of Wild Red Sea Bream Pagrus major in Different Water Temperatures
evidence.method: One wild adult tracked for 28 days with an ultrasonic transmitter; ambient temperature and vertical movement recorded.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The fish encountered 18.5-22.9 degC and stayed near a shoal; temperature fluctuation appeared to have little effect on swimming behavior.
evidence.rejectionReason: Encountered temperature is not a selected or preferred range; n=1.

evidence.sourceTitle: Correlation of changes in seasonal distribution and catch of red sea bream Pagrus major with winter temperature in the eastern Seto Inland Sea, Japan (1972-2010)
evidence.method: Long-term catch and seasonal distribution correlated with winter temperature at 10 m.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Winter distribution and catch expanded in warmer years; temperatures below roughly 8 degC were unfavorable.
evidence.rejectionReason: Catch correlation and a lower threshold do not define a preferred min/max range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Acoustic Telemetrical Tracking of the Response Behavior of Red Seabream to Artificial Reefs
evidence.publisherOrJournal: Korean Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 37(5):433-439
evidence.wildCaptiveContext: field release; origin not established in accessible contract
evidence.method: Acoustic telemetry of movement and diel behavior around artificial reefs.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The study reports movement between deep and shallow water and reef response, not thermal selection.
evidence.rejectionReason: No numeric temperature range and no temperature-selection analysis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Movement range and behavior characteristics of Pagrus major by acoustic telemetry in Byeonsan Peninsular, Korea
evidence.publisherOrJournal: Journal of the Korean Society of Fisheries and Ocean Technology 57(1):34-44
evidence.method: Four cultured fish, mean TL 27.1 cm, tracked around pile-driving work.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The experiment addresses movement response to construction activity.
evidence.rejectionReason: Cultured fish, short tracking, no preferred-temperature range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Movement pattern of red seabream Pagrus major and yellowtail Seriola quinqueradiata around Offshore Wind Turbine and neighboring habitats
evidence.wildCaptiveContext: field-tagged; origin not sufficient for strict transfer
evidence.method: Acoustic telemetry around offshore wind turbine and adjacent habitats in winter and summer.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Residency and movement around structures were measured.
evidence.rejectionReason: No numeric temperature range or thermal selection analysis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Experimental study on temperature preference of Japanese marine fish
evidence.method: Horizontal temperature-gradient preference experiment across acclimation treatments.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Explicit acclimation-dependent preference range and final preferendum were reported.
evidence.rejectionReason: Juvenile-only laboratory evidence cannot establish adult general wild preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Survival and Physiological Responses of Red Sea Bream Pagrus major with Decreasing Sea Water Temperature
evidence.method: Progressive cooling and seven-day lethal-temperature analysis.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Seven-day LT50 was 6.54 degC.
evidence.rejectionReason: Lethal tolerance in captivity is not preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Temperature Responses of Young Schlegel's Black Rockfish Sebastes schlegelii
evidence.method: Horizontal temperature-gradient preference test across 15-28 degC acclimation groups.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Preferred temperature was 17.8-22.8 degC and final preferendum about 20.5 degC.
evidence.rejectionReason: Young-fish laboratory scope does not establish adult wild preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Short-Term Fidelity, Habitat Use and Vertical Movement Behavior of the Black Rockfish Sebastes schlegelii as Determined by Acoustic Telemetry
evidence.method: Acoustic telemetry and habitat selection index over up to 46 days.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Selection was demonstrated for reef and substrate classes, not for temperature.
evidence.rejectionReason: The selected variable was substrate; no numeric selected-temperature range was estimated.

evidence.sourceTitle: Home ranges and homing routes of black rockfish Sebastes schlegelii measured by acoustic telemetry
evidence.publisherOrJournal: Korean Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 41(3):221-227
evidence.method: Twenty-four fish released at five distances and tracked acoustically for homing.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Homing range and routes were evaluated.
evidence.rejectionReason: No numeric preferred-temperature range or selection analysis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Short-Term Movement of MiniPAT-Tagged Coastal Fishes in the Yellow Sea: Case Studies on Korean Rockfish and Spotted Sea Bass
evidence.wildCaptiveContext: field-tagged; capture/origin context not sufficient in accessible abstract
evidence.method: Two 33.0-34.1 cm Korean rockfish tracked with external miniPATs for 5-12 days.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Individuals experienced mean ambient temperatures of 24.15 +/- 1.20 and 17.99 +/- 2.68 degC.
evidence.rejectionReason: Individual means are observed exposure, not a selected population min/max range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Predicting current and future global distribution of black rockfish Sebastes schlegelii under changing climate
evidence.method: Ensemble species-distribution models using bottom temperature and other predictors.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Bottom temperature was the most important predictor of modelled habitat suitability.
evidence.rejectionReason: Modelled distribution is not observed behavioral preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Deep Transcriptomic Analysis of Black Rockfish Sebastes schlegelii Provides New Insights on Responses to Acute Temperature Stress
evidence.method: Acute low/control/high temperature challenge with liver transcriptomics.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The paper cites 18-24 degC as an optimal range while testing acute thermal stress in cultured adults.
evidence.rejectionReason: Secondary aquaculture optimum and captive stress response are not wild selection.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effect of Rearing Temperature on Growth and Maturation of Black Rockfish Sebastes schlegelii
evidence.method: Fish reared from 7 to 48 months under natural, 12 degC, and 15 degC winter-spring conditions.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Growth and maturation responses to managed rearing temperatures were tested.
evidence.rejectionReason: Managed rearing treatments do not establish wild preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Horizontal and vertical movement of yellowtails Seriola quinqueradiata during summer to early winter recorded by archival tags in the northeastern Japan Sea
evidence.method: Twenty-six adults 61-90 cm FL tagged; eight recaptured after more than two months with temperature records every 60 or 120 seconds.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Fish primarily occupied the mixed layer, made dives, and avoided cold offshore water during southward movement.
evidence.rejectionReason: Cold avoidance and encountered temperatures were not converted by the study into an explicit selected min/max range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Migration of the adult yellowtail Seriola quinqueradiata as estimated by archival tagging experiments in the Tsushima Warm Current
evidence.publisherOrJournal: Bulletin of the Japanese Society of Fisheries Oceanography 72(2):92-100
evidence.geographicContext: Tsushima Warm Current, Japan Sea and East China Sea
evidence.method: 138 tagged; positions estimated for 26 recaptured fish aged four years and older.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Three adult migration patterns and likely spawning movements were identified.
evidence.rejectionReason: Accessible full contract does not provide a numeric selected-temperature range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Horizontal and vertical movement patterns of yellowtail Seriola quinqueradiata in the East Sea of Korea
authors: Korean Institute of Ocean Science and Technology research team
evidence.geographicContext: South and East Seas of Korea
evidence.wildCaptiveContext: commercially sourced and sea-cage held before field release
evidence.method: Two 8.7 and 9.5 kg fish monitored by PSAT; one record lasted 82 days.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The long record had mean ambient temperature 16.52 +/- 1.86 degC; a 12-day fish averaged 20.65 +/- 0.36 degC.
evidence.rejectionReason: Observed means from two pre-held fish are not a preferred min/max range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Growth and Food Consumption in Young Amber-Fish, Seriola quinqueradiata
evidence.wildCaptiveContext: wild fisheries context plus feeding experiments
evidence.method: Field samples and feeding experiments; introduction states schools select coastal waters of 10-20 degC.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The paper explicitly states that the species usually migrates in schools selecting 10-20 degC coastal waters.
evidence.rejectionReason: The range is a background assertion without a documented selection analysis or clear adult/general derivation in the paper.

evidence.sourceTitle: Response of yellowtail, Seriola quinqueradiata, to sea water temperature over the last century and potential effects of global warming
evidence.method: Long-term catch/distribution analysis and habitat mapping against sea temperature.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Yellowtail abundance and distribution were associated with temperature and projected warming.
evidence.rejectionReason: Modelled suitable habitat and catch response are not direct behavioral preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Movement pattern of red seabream Pagrus major and yellowtail Seriola quinqueradiata around Offshore Wind Turbine and neighboring habitats
evidence.wildCaptiveContext: field-tagged; origin not sufficient in abstract
evidence.method: Twenty yellowtail acoustically tracked around an offshore wind turbine and neighboring reefs/FADs in summer.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Residence time and structure use were measured.
evidence.rejectionReason: No numeric temperature range or temperature-selection analysis.

evidence.sourceTitle: Experimental study on temperature preference of Japanese marine fish
evidence.method: Horizontal temperature-gradient preference experiment across acclimation treatments.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: Explicit acclimation-dependent preference range and final preferendum were reported.
evidence.rejectionReason: Juvenile-only laboratory evidence cannot establish adult general wild preference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Cultured Aquatic Species Information Programme: Seriola quinqueradiata
evidence.publisherOrJournal: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
evidence.method: Culture-practice synthesis.
evidence.sourceStatementSummary: The fact sheet identifies 20-29 degC as optimum rearing temperature.
evidence.rejectionReason: Rearing optimum is not adult wild preference.
